scope: Exact frozen 12 candidate files and direct consumers only; SOURCE and artifact identity review; no PG/native runtime/provider/network/model/credentials/profile/repository writes.

findings.title: Schema unavailability short-circuits known invalid artifact validation
findings.actual: Resealed operations="not-an-array" refuses METHOD_SCHEMA_MISMATCH with all qualified schemas. Delete only the input schema; identical malformed operations output now produces UNKNOWN/all three gaps rather than refusing. Valid output with missing input schema produces UNKNOWN as intended.
findings.impact: UNKNOWN fallback bypasses validation of later artifacts whose schemas remain available; malformed execution is represented as an eligible UNKNOWN check, not a contract/schema error. No COMPLETE or N/A escalation demonstrated. Owner also discards all schema documents on its first unavailable schema.
findings.requirement: Invalid schema/value/identity must remain refusal; unavailable qualification may produce UNKNOWN, but must not mask a separately decidable mismatch.
findings.remedy: Accumulate unavailable qualification per item, continue validating every available schema/value, prioritize any mismatch refusal. Preserve partial schema material in the owner instead of replacing it wholesale with {}. Add mixed missing+invalid negative in both orders.

findings.title: Malformed checker descriptors are normalized to unavailable UNKNOWN
findings.actual: Current descriptor changed only to semantics=false, semantics={unexpected:object}, or code_digest="not-a-sha256" each yields UNKNOWN, METHOD_CHECKER_UNAVAILABLE and three gaps.
findings.impact: The new catch widens well-formed unavailable identity handling to schema/type-invalid descriptors. No COMPLETE escalation demonstrated.
findings.requirement: Strict checker identity/schema validation must precede the unavailable fallback; SHA identifier syntax and semantic text type must not be repaired/treated as missing eligibility.
findings.remedy: Validate exact descriptor field types, digest syntax/length and bounded semantic text before identity lookup. Use a distinct malformed-descriptor error not caught as METHOD_CHECKER_UNAVAILABLE; preserve UNKNOWN for well-formed unknown identities.

findings.title: Allocated criterion consumer still rejects UNKNOWN and rolls back check publication
findings.actual: Same otherwise-valid two-criterion fixture produces two BLOCKED outcomes and METHOD_INCOMPLETE gaps for INCOMPLETE; UNKNOWN refuses CRITERION_CHECK_REQUIRED.
findings.impact: _check stores the new check and then calls this consumer within one transaction. With allocated criteria UNKNOWN cannot settle a check/outcome/inbox; native UNKNOWN author QA intentionally selected no allocation. This is a confirmed direct-consumer integration gap, not false success.
findings.requirement: New UNKNOWN result must propagate conservatively through existing allocated outcomes and remain non-successful.
findings.remedy: Permit UNKNOWN at this direct consumer, include explicit method uncertainty gap and retain BLOCKED/no PASS; add allocation-bearing SOURCE and affected native/PG consumer QA. No change to observer/guard/deadlines.

findings.title: New catalog applicability behavior is outside compiler/evaluator fingerprint closure
findings.actual: _compile_catalog newly invokes tasks.managed_contract.requirement_conditions, but BEHAVIOR_FILES omits tasks/managed_contract.py. The real behavior_revision called with a virtual reader that changes only that source returns identical compiler identity and never reads the changed module (0 reads). No repository bytes changed.
findings.impact: Two distributions differing in the trusted applicability validator can share COMPILER_REVISION/EVALUATOR_REVISION and thus qualification identity. Checker closure includes the file, but does not repair candidate compilation/evaluation closure.
findings.requirement: Fingerprint closure must cover executable trusted compiler/evaluator behavior used for qualification/publication.
findings.remedy: Extend candidate behavior closure to include the newly invoked validator and its trusted transitive behavior dependencies, or move this finite validation into an already-hashed shared module. Add behavioral dependency closure regression and reconcile newly minted qualification identities; do not silently promote historical records.
